Because of the manufacturers' voluntary use of lighter six cylinder and V-8 engines, a one-time savings in steel and cast iron of 17.1 million pounds is likely to result with an attendant savings in energy equivalent in BTU's to 50,100 barrels of oil. A small improvement in water quality, a small decrease in industrial water supply demand and a small reduction in stationary source air pollution will likely result from the decreased use of cast iron and steel. The adverse impact discussed previously regarding the increased use of platinum and palladium also applies.
With regard to the second alternative, before the agency can set standards for any group of automobiles, it must have data establishing a baseline level of average fuel economy for the group.
